Subject: Pilot efficiency package & quant recommendations — follow-up

Hi Ellen —

Thanks again for the call this morning. I attached a concise pilot proposal (Optimize_Pilot_Proposal_v1.pdf) and a short spreadsheet with the quantization and latency estimates (quantization-recommendations.xlsx). TL;DR on our recommendation and a slightly flexible commercial option to help finalize procurement: 

- Recommended pilot scope: 3 months, 50k prompts/month (mixed short and medium sequences), 1 production route for user-facing chat and 1 route for batch inference.
- Performance levers: enable prefix KV caching on the chat route, set conservative batching window (10–30ms) for low-variance latency, and apply mixed quantization profile (int8 for latency-critical, int4 for background/high-throughput).
- Commercial proposal: 15% pilot discount off list, $10k pilot credit for testing ops, and straightforward conversion pricing with a 12-month commitment discount (20%) if you convert before pilot end.

Ask: could you share the procurement timeline and whether Acme needs an SOW/PO template? Also let us know if the quantization/accuracy tradeoff above matches your expectations; Aditya and Connor are looped for any technical follow-up.

Next steps: If this looks good, I can send a short SOW and a revised proposal with explicit SLA language and SOC2 evidence links. Would you be available for a 30-minute alignment on Tuesday?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett

Appreciate the notes and the quick turnaround. A few clarifying questions from our side before we kick procurement:

2) Support & SLA: for the pilot, what level of response time should we expect (P1/P2), and is there an option to include a dedicated onboarding session?
3) Accuracy: can you quantify expected model delta for int4 on our workload? Our clinical triage prompts are sensitive to hallucination risk.

Hi Ellen —

Answers inline: 

1) Discounting: the 15% pilot discount is our standard for defined pilots but we can flex based on commit and usage. If you convert to a 12-month commit at >= 250k tokens/month before the pilot ends, we move to 20% on the converted term. We can also tier usage bands (250k+, 500k+, 1M+) for deeper discounts — happy to enumerate in the SOW.

2) Support & SLA: pilot includes business-hours support with a 4-hour P1 response target. For an add-on fee we can provide 24/7 P1 coverage and a kickoff workshop (2 half-days) that includes performance tuning and playbook walkthrough. I'll include both options in the SOW.

3) Accuracy and quantization: based on the prompt samples you shared on the call, our lab estimates for int4 (post-quant) show model KL/quality shifts of approximately 0.5–1.5% on classification-like metrics; for generation fidelity we recommend using int8 for the chat route and int4 for high-throughput batch where micro hallucinations are less risky. We've attached quantization-recommendations.xlsx with per-prompt-category deltas. Important caveats: 
  - Run a short A/B eval set (we suggest 1k representative prompts) during pilot to confirm deltas in your live data.
  - KV-cache warmup can cause a small initial latency spike; see Aditya's note below for pre-warm suggestions.

Commercial sweetener: Redwood is prepared to provide a $10k pilot credit if Acme signs the conversion commit within 30 days of pilot end. That credit is applied to the first invoice after conversion.

Connor and Aditya — can you confirm SOC2 artifact link and whether we should include a short security appendix in the SOW?

Ellen — I will draft the SOW and revised proposal (including explicit discount tiers and SLA options) and share by EOD.

Best,
Laura

Subject: Re: Pilot efficiency package & quant recommendations — technical notes

Quick technical addendum from the runtime side: 

- KV-cache warmup: for chat routes we recommend a pre-warm job that replays representative sessions to populate prefix caches; this avoids the cold-start 50–200ms tail. We can provide a small script and runbook as part of onboarding.
- Batching: set target batch windows by route — 15ms for low-latency chat (max 8 requests per batch), 50–200ms for batch inference (higher batch sizes) to maximize throughput.
- Quantization details: we support both static INT8 and mixed INT4 pipelines. For models where hallucination risk is high, keep logits in FP16 during generation while applying int4 to most linear layers; this preserves sampling fidelity.
- Ops concession: we can include a one-time $10k pilot credit (applied against invoices) and a free 4-hour tuning session with the infra team.

Happy to run a short, reproducible A/B script against your sample set — should take ~2 business days to run and produce the per-prompt deltas you asked about.

— Aditya
